standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic transportation costs task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: In the fictional town of Elm Crossing, a Saturday volunteer shift at the Elm Crossing Food Pantry is followed by a stop at the library on the way home.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l02-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l02-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l02-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l02-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Would the day pass still be the cheapest choice if the volunteer only needed two ride legs instead of three? Explain your reasoning using the fare numbers.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g8-u04-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Cost calculation accuracy: All three totals are calculated correctly using the given fare numbers and the correct count of three ride legs. | Comparative reasoning and justification: Names the least expensive option and explains the choice by directly comparing the calculated totals for this specific three-leg trip. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner add a fourth fictional ride leg to the plan and recalculate all three totals to see whether the cheapest option changes.

resources.title: transportation costs worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: In the fictional town of Elm Crossing, a Saturday volunteer shift at the Elm Crossing Food Pantry is followed by a stop at the library on the way home.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact transportation costs decision or action.
Model move 2: Compare the two fictional fares for a single ride before looking at the whole trip.
Model move 3: Count how many separate ride legs the full trip actually requires before comparing totals.

Model check: Cost calculation accuracy: All three totals are calculated correctly using the given fare numbers and the correct count of three ride legs. | Comparative reasoning and justification: Names the least expensive option and explains the choice by directly comparing the calculated totals for this specific three-leg trip.

resources.title: transportation costs action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for transportation costs.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: transportation costs coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: In the fictional town of Elm Crossing, a Saturday volunteer shift at the Elm Crossing Food Pantry is followed by a stop at the library on the way home.
Coach direction: Compare the two fictional fares for a single ride before looking at the whole trip.

Learner prompt: A Crosstown Circuit single ride costs $1.75 and a day pass costs $4.00. A QuickHop ride costs a flat $6.25 no matter the distance within Elm Crossing. If the volunteer only needed one ride today, which option costs less, and by how much?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: transportation costs complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Count how many separate ride legs the full trip actually requires before comparing totals.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I counted three separate ride legs: home to pantry, pantry to library, and library to home.
Response 2 (t2-p2): What is the total Crosstown Circuit cost if the volunteer buys three single rides instead of a day pass?
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: transportation costs minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Would the day pass still be the cheapest choice if the volunteer only needed two ride legs instead of three? Explain your reasoning using the fare numbers.

Success checks: Cost calculation accuracy: All three totals are calculated correctly using the given fare numbers and the correct count of three ride legs. | Comparative reasoning and justification: Names the least expensive option and explains the choice by directly comparing the calculated totals for this specific three-leg trip.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: transportation costs supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g8-u04-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional transportation costs condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Cost calculation accuracy: All three totals are calculated correctly using the given fare numbers and the correct count of three ride legs. | Comparative reasoning and justification: Names the least expensive option and explains the choice by directly comparing the calculated totals for this specific three-leg trip..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.title: transportation costs — complete fictional route

simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
